target_customer: Large financial institutions and market infrastructure providers (banks, DTCC, exchanges) needing shared multi-party data and post-trade workflows
problem: Banks keep separate copies of trade data and spend heavily on reconciliation. Axoni builds distributed data replication and workflow infrastructure so counterparties share a single source of truth. At the YC batch the founders ran TradeBlock, a bitcoin data and trading tools business.
business_model: Enterprise software and infrastructure licensing plus services to financial institutions
product_category: Enterprise blockchain and data replication infrastructure

founders.name: Greg Schvey
founders.background_notes: Fixed income analyst at Citigroup per the YC page.

founders.name: Jeffrey Schvey
founders.background_notes: Engineering lead in Raytheon's strategy group per the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Distributed ledger and high-throughput data replication for financial workflows with strict reliability needs is hard for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Bank consortium investors and deployed multi-party networks such as the DTCC credit default swap warehouse create strong lock-in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent absorbed the business in sources found; banks invested instead.

market_need_then: In 2014 the batch company, TradeBlock, served institutional bitcoin data demand and was called the Bloomberg of bitcoin by AlleyWatch. The Axoni distributed ledger need for derivatives emerged around 2016.

branding.domain_note: Uses axoni.com; no acquisition history found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Tagline: the easiest way to share and consume critical data; values enthusiasm, integrity and performance (company site)

rebrands.why: Founders launched Axoni as a distinct permissioned ledger venture

branding.community_and_virality: Company site cites coverage in WSJ, Forbes, Bloomberg, Reuters and CNBC and Forbes Fintech 50; no consumer community.

brand_strength.rationale: Respected in capital markets circles per press logos, but it is an enterprise brand with no evidence the name drove growth.

pivots.from: TradeBlock bitcoin market data and trading tools
pivots.to: Axoni permissioned distributed ledger infrastructure for financial institutions
pivots.why: Founders launched a new venture to serve institutional financial workflows; reason beyond that not stated in sources opened

outcome_analysis: The founders entered YC with TradeBlock, raised $2.8M led by Andreessen Horowitz in July 2014, then spun out Axoni around 2016 and sold distributed ledger infrastructure to banks. A string of bank-backed rounds followed, an $18M Series A in 2016, a $32M Series B in 2018, a $31M extension in 2021 and about $20M in 2023, and the company appears to remain independent with 155 people.
notes: The directory and YC page say Acquired but no acquirer or deal was found; Employbl lists Axoni as not acquired with Greg Schvey as CEO, so exit is recorded unknown. The YC batch company was TradeBlock; the 2014 $2.8M a16z-led TradeBlock round (July 2014, per AlleyWatch URL path) is not an Axoni round and is not listed. Funding totals conflict: Global Venturing says $90M by 2021 while aggregators say $110M to $128M. The 2023 round is labeled other since sources disagree on stage (Series C or B). Competitors dated near 2014 were not found; the sources opened name none.
